quote: Asana or posture gives Driddhata or strength; Mudra gives Sthirata or steadiness; Pratyahara gives Dhairyata or calmness; Pranayama gives lightness or Laghima.
who: The sage Gheranda
source: Gheranda Samhita 1.10-11 (Lesson First), tr. Rai Bahadur Srisa Chandra Vasu, The Gheranda Samhita (Panini Office, Allahabad, 1914; Gheranda title page dated 1914), bound in Sacred Books of the Hindus vol. 15 (volume title page 1915), printed p. 3
meaning: Asana builds strength, mudra steadiness, pratyahara calm, and pranayama lightness.
credit: Gheranda Samhita 1.10-11 · tr. S. C. Vasu

quote: Perform action, O Dhananjaya, dwelling in union with the divine, renouncing attachments and balanced evenly in success and failure: equilibrium is called yoga.
who: Krishna, in the Bhagavad Gita
source: Bhagavad Gita 2.48, tr. Annie Besant, The Bhagavad-Gita, 4th ed., 1922 (Wikisource transcription of the scanned edition)
meaning: Do your work and stay steady in success or failure; that steadiness is yoga.

quote: Earnest among the thoughtless, awake among the sleepers, the wise man advances like a racer, leaving behind the hack.
who: The Buddha
source: Dhammapada 29 (ch. II, 'On Earnestness'), tr. F. Max Müller, Sacred Books of the East vol. 10, 1881 (Project Gutenberg eBook #2017)
meaning: Stay wide awake while others doze, and you move ahead like a fast horse.
credit: The Buddha · Dhammapada 29, tr. Max Müller

quote: By the practice of the different parts of Yogas the impurities being destroyed, knowledge becomes effulgent up to discrimination.
who: Patanjali
source: Yoga Sutra 2.28, tr. Swami Vivekananda, Raja Yoga (1896), in The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, vol. 1 (Wikisource)
meaning: As you practise the limbs of yoga, impurity fades and clear knowing shines.

quote: From that, the covering to the light of the Chitta is attenuated. The mind becomes fit for Dharana.
who: Patanjali
source: Yoga Sutra 2.52-53, tr. Swami Vivekananda, Raja Yoga (1896), in The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda, vol. 1 (Wikisource)
meaning: Breath practice clears the mind and makes it ready to focus.

quote: Therefore, the body, sense organs, and mind must be stabilized to prevent obstacles ... from occurring.
who: K. Pattabhi Jois
source: Yoga Mala, end of the 'Niyama' chapter: the paragraph right after Ishwarapranidhana (Yoga Sutra 2.45), where asana is introduced, before the 'Pranayama' chapter. Written in Kannada 1958-c.1961, first published 1962; English tr. Sri Vishwanath Kadam and Dr. H. L. Chandrashekar, ed. Deirdre Summerbell; North Point Press 2002, new ed. 2010. Page not checked.
meaning: Keep body, senses and mind steady so problems are stopped before they start.

quote: ...only by being prepared to suffer any obstacles that we may encounter along the way will we then accrue the desired benefits. If you leave it halfway, it is like falling down.
who: T. Krishnamacharya
source: Yoga Makaranda (Kannada ed. 1934; Tamil ed. 1938), ch. 1.5 'Who has the authority to practise Yoga', p. 18; English tr. Lakshmi Ranganathan and Nandini Ranganathan, 2006
meaning: Be ready to meet obstacles on the way, and do not stop halfway.

quote: Shariramadyam khalu dharma sadhanam [The first duty is to take care of the body, which is the means to the pursuit of spiritual life].
who: K. Pattabhi Jois, quoting 'the great sages' (the line is from Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava 5.33)
source: Yoga Mala, chapter 'Surya Namaskara and Yoga Asanas', introduction to Surya Namaskara; English tr. Kadam and Chandrashekar (North Point Press 2002/2010). Sanskrit verse checked in GRETIL, Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava, line Ks_5.33 (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de/gretil/corpustei/transformations/plaintext/sa_kAlidAsa-kumArasaMbhava.txt). Page not checked.
meaning: Caring for your body comes first; it is how you walk the spiritual path.
credit: K. P. Jois quoting Kalidasa · Yoga Mala

quote: ...the bodies of sadhakas will become as strong as diamonds through the practice of yoga. They should therefore not allow themselves to become indifferent, but should pursue their practices with faith and reverence.
who: K. Pattabhi Jois
source: Yoga Mala, 'Yoga Asanas', no. 15 'Janu Shirshasana (A)'; English tr. Kadam and Chandrashekar (North Point Press 2002/2010). Page not checked.
meaning: Keep practising with respect, and yoga makes your body strong as a diamond.

quote: When you want to go deeper, just like when you reach deep into a jungle, you are bound to face many challenges. The important thing is to remember that this is temporary, and you will emerge on the other side stronger.
who: R. Sharath Jois
source: R. Sharath Jois with Isha Singh Sawhney, Ageless: A Yogi's Secrets to a Long and Healthy Life (Juggernaut Books, 2018), Introduction, p. xvii
meaning: Going deep brings challenges, but they pass, and you come out stronger.

quote: Every day is a good day.
who: Yunmen Wenyan (d. 949), Chan (Zen) master
source: Blue Cliff Record (Biyan lu, compiled 1125), case 6: Yunmen asks for one line about the days after the fifteenth, then answers for his monks: 日日是好日. Literal translation. Dictionary sources on Kotobank: デジタル大辞泉 ('every day is a peaceful, good day', from the Blue Cliff Record); 故事成語を知る辞典 (traces it to 碧巌録 case 6); 精選版 日本国語大辞典 (earliest Japanese use: 大燈国師語録, 1426).
meaning: Every day is a good day, just as it comes.

quote: If only you knew where you would fall, you would spread a little straw there.
who: Russian proverb
source: V. I. Dal, Poslovitsy russkogo naroda (Proverbs of the Russian People), 1862 (academic.ru text of the 1989 Khudozhestvennaya literatura edition), rubric ОПЛОШНОСТЬ — РАСТОРОПНОСТЬ. Literal translation. Dal also lists 'Кабы знать, где упасть, так соломки б подостлал' under СЧАСТЬЕ — УДАЧА and 'Знать бы, где пасть, так бы соломки подостлать' under БЫЛОЕ — БУДУЩЕЕ.
meaning: Nobody knows where they will fall, or they would put straw there first.

quote: The perfect man employs his mind as a mirror. It grasps nothing: it refuses nothing. It receives, but does not keep.
who: Zhuangzi (Chuang Tzu), Daoist philosopher, 4th century BCE
source: Zhuangzi, ch. 7 (應帝王), closing section, tr. Herbert A. Giles, Chuang Tzŭ: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer, London: Bernard Quaritch, 1889, ch. VII, p. 98 area (public domain, Wikisource). Chinese text checked on zh.wikisource 莊子/應帝王.
meaning: Let your mind be like a mirror: meet everything, hold on to nothing.
credit: Zhuangzi · ch. 7, tr. H. A. Giles, 1889

quote: Patience and work will grind through everything.
who: Russian proverb
source: V. I. Dal, Poslovitsy russkogo naroda (Proverbs of the Russian People), 1862 (academic.ru text of the 1989 edition), rubric ТЕРПЕНИЕ — НАДЕЖДА. Literal translation. Also in Mikhelson's Bolshoi tolkovo-frazeologichesky slovar.
meaning: Patience and steady work wear down every hard thing, bit by bit.

quote: ...we should not move the body without the soul or the soul without the body, and thus they will be on their guard against each other, and be healthy and well balanced.
who: Plato (spoken by the character Timaeus)
source: Plato, Timaeus 88b, tr. Benjamin Jowett (1871; 3rd ed. 1892)
meaning: Train body and mind together, so both stay healthy and balanced.

quote: You must conform to rules, submit to a diet, refrain from dainties; exercise your body, whether you choose it or not, at a stated hour, in heat and cold...
who: Epictetus, Stoic teacher (c. 50-135)
source: Enchiridion (Handbook) 29, tr. Thomas W. Higginson, 1865 (Liberal Arts Press reprint, 1948)
meaning: Big goals mean training at a set hour, in heat and cold.

quote: The art of life is more like the wrestler's art than the dancer's, in respect of this, that it should stand ready and firm to meet onsets which are sudden and unexpected.
who: Marcus Aurelius, Stoic philosopher (121-180)
source: Meditations (Thoughts) VII.61, tr. George Long, 1862
meaning: Living is like wrestling: stay steady and ready for sudden surprises.

quote: Every morning was a cheerful invitation to make my life of equal simplicity, and I may say innocence, with Nature herself.
who: Henry David Thoreau, American writer (1817-1862)
source: Walden, 1854, chapter 'Where I Lived, and What I Lived For'
meaning: Each new morning invited him to live simply, like nature itself.

quote: ...have you not received faculties by which you will be able to bear all that happens? Have you not received greatness of soul? ... Have you not received endurance?
who: Epictetus, Stoic teacher (c. 50-135)
source: Discourses I.6 ('Of Providence'), tr. George Long, 1877 (from Long's 'A Selection from the Discourses of Epictetus with the Encheiridion')
meaning: You already have the inner strength to handle whatever happens.
credit: Epictetus · Discourses I.6, tr. George Long

quote: ...the equipment of an expedition such as we were about to enter upon is not the affair of a day... Victory awaits him who has everything in order -- luck, people call it.
who: Roald Amundsen, polar explorer
source: Roald Amundsen, The South Pole: An Account of the Norwegian Antarctic Expedition in the 'Fram', 1910-1912, Vol. 1, ch. IX 'The End of the Winter', tr. A. G. Chater (London: John Murray, 1912). Public domain.
meaning: Getting ready takes a long time. People call it luck; it is preparation.

quote: ...20 years previously we had started studying Russian... and then we got into the simulator and practiced over and over and over again... we weren't screaming, we were laughing; it was fun.
who: Chris Hadfield, on coming home in a Soyuz capsule, May 2013
source: Chris Hadfield, 'What I learned from going blind in space', TED2014, Vancouver, recorded 18 March 2014 (official TED transcript).
meaning: Years of practice, over and over, turned a wild ride home into fun.

quote: If you undertrain, you might not finish. If you overtrain, you might not start.
who: Olga Kotelko, Canadian masters track athlete (took up track at 77; aged 91 in 2010)
source: Bruce Grierson, 'The Incredible Flying Nonagenarian', The New York Times Magazine, 28 November 2010 (reposted on the author's site, credited 'THE NEW YORK TIMES MAGAZINE, Nov. 28, 2010').
meaning: Too little training, you may not finish; too much, you may not start.

quote: It makes me feel internally and physically strong... But to get to that point, you must practise.
who: Willem Dafoe, actor, on his morning ashtanga vinyasa practice
source: Chris Cotonou, 'Willem Dafoe: Acting is like being a colour in an artist's palette', A Rabbit's Foot magazine, 6 March 2024.
meaning: His morning Ashtanga makes him strong inside and out, but you must practise.

quote: ...allostasis, maintaining stability through change, as a fundamental process through which organisms actively adjust to both predictable and unpredictable events.
who: Bruce S. McEwen (Rockefeller University) and John C. Wingfield, biologists of stress
source: McEwen BS, Wingfield JC. The concept of allostasis in biology and biomedicine. Hormones and Behavior, 2003;43(1):2-15. doi:10.1016/s0018-506x(02)00024-7. PMID 12614627 (abstract).
meaning: Living bodies stay steady by adjusting to change, expected or unexpected.

quote: A newer model, "allostasis", proposes that efficient regulation requires anticipating needs and preparing to satisfy them before they arise.
who: Peter Sterling, neuroscientist, University of Pennsylvania
source: Sterling P. Allostasis: a model of predictive regulation. Physiology & Behavior, 2012;106(1):5-15 (online 12 June 2011). doi:10.1016/j.physbeh.2011.06.004. PMID 21684297 (abstract).
meaning: The brain keeps the body efficient by preparing for needs before they arise.

quote: ...fit individuals showed significantly attenuated heart rate and systolic blood pressure reactivity... Fit individuals also showed faster heart rate recovery...
who: Kathleen Forcier, Laura R. Stroud and colleagues, Brown Medical School
source: Forcier K, Stroud LR, Papandonatos GD, Hitsman B, Reiches M, Krishnamoorthy J, Niaura R. Links between physical fitness and cardiovascular reactivity and recovery to psychological stressors: A meta-analysis. Health Psychology, 2006;25(6):723-739. doi:10.1037/0278-6133.25.6.723. PMID 17100501 (abstract).
meaning: Fit people's hearts react less to stress and settle down faster after.

quote: Exercise reduces the rate of falls by 23%... balance and functional exercises reduce the rate of falls by 24%...
who: Catherine Sherrington and colleagues, University of Sydney (Cochrane review)
source: Sherrington C, Fairhall NJ, Wallbank GK, Tiedemann A, Michaleff ZA, Howard K, Clemson L, Hopewell S, Lamb SE. Exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2019, Issue 1, CD012424. doi:10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub2. PMID 30703272 (abstract).
meaning: Exercise with balance work helped people over 60 fall about a quarter less.

quote: ...increased comfort, relaxation, pleasantness, vigor and alertness...
who: Andrea Zaccaro and colleagues, University of Pisa
source: Zaccaro A, Piarulli A, Laurino M, Garbella E, Menicucci D, Neri B, Gemignani A. How Breath-Control Can Change Your Life: A Systematic Review on Psycho-Physiological Correlates of Slow Breathing. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2018;12:353 (online 7 Sep 2018). doi:10.3389/fnhum.2018.00353. PMC6137615.
meaning: Slow breathing, under 10 breaths a minute, helps people feel relaxed and alert.
credit: Zaccaro et al. · Front Hum Neurosci, 2018

quote: ...yoga practitioners (i) were more accurate in assessing the rod's verticality...
who: Francesca Fiori, Nicole David, Salvatore M. Aglioti, Sapienza University of Rome
source: Fiori F, David N, Aglioti SM. Processing of proprioceptive and vestibular body signals and self-transcendence in Ashtanga yoga practitioners. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2014;8:734. doi:10.3389/fnhum.2014.00734. PMC4166896.
meaning: Ashtanga practitioners judged 'straight up' more accurately than non-yoga peers.
credit: Fiori et al. · Front Hum Neurosci, 2014

quote: Learn thou from him who tore green branches down, / That tasks deferred are wrought in tears at last.
who: The Bodhisatta as a teacher of 500 pupils, in a Jataka tale told by the Buddha
source: Varana Jataka, No. 71, tr. Robert Chalmers, in The Jataka, vol. I, ed. E. B. Cowell, Cambridge University Press, 1895, pp. 172-174
meaning: Do the job early. Jobs left to the last minute end in tears.

quote: The utility of this science consists in the maintenance of health in the healthy and in the quieting of disorders in the ailing.
who: Charaka Samhita (teaching of Atreya, compiled by Agnivesha, revised by Charaka)
source: Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 30.26, tr. Shree Gulabkunverba Ayurvedic Society, Jamnagar, 1949 (wisdomlib transcription)
meaning: Ayurveda has two jobs: keep healthy people healthy, and help sick people heal.

quote: Compressing his breathings let him, who has subdued all motions, breathe forth through the nose with gentle breath. Let the wise man without fail restrain his mind, that chariot yoked with vicious horses.
who: Svetasvatara Upanishad
source: Svetasvatara Upanishad II.9, tr. F. Max Müller, The Upanishads Part II, Sacred Books of the East vol. 15, Oxford, 1884, p. 241
meaning: Breathe gently through the nose and keep steady hold of your restless mind.

quote: Nor is that Self to be gained by one who is destitute of strength, or without earnestness, or without right meditation.
who: Mundaka Upanishad (teaching of the sage Angiras to Shaunaka)
source: Mundaka Upanishad III.2.4, tr. F. Max Müller, The Upanishads Part II, Sacred Books of the East vol. 15, Oxford, 1884, p. 40
meaning: Finding your true self takes strength, steady care and right meditation.

quote: This, the firm holding back of the senses, is what is called Yoga. He must be free from thoughtlessness then, for Yoga comes and goes.
who: Yama, teaching Nachiketas, in the Katha Upanishad
source: Katha Upanishad II.6.11 (= 2.3.11 in modern numbering), tr. F. Max Müller, The Upanishads Part II, Sacred Books of the East vol. 15, Oxford, 1884, p. 22
meaning: Yoga means holding the senses steady. Stay alert, because yoga comes and goes.

quote: We are a little piece of continual change looking at an infinite quantity of continual change.
who: B. K. S. Iyengar, yoga teacher, Pune
source: B. K. S. Iyengar with John J. Evans and Douglas Abrams, Light on Life: The Yoga Journey to Wholeness, Inner Peace, and Ultimate Freedom (Emmaus, PA: Rodale, 2005), ch. 1 'The Inward Journey'; p. 7 in the 2006 Rodale printing (page per Wikiquote)
meaning: We keep changing, and we look at a world that keeps changing too.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Life, 2005

quote: If you can adapt to and balance in a world that is always moving and unstable, you learn how to become tolerant to the permanence of change and difference.
who: B. K. S. Iyengar, yoga teacher, Pune
source: B. K. S. Iyengar with John J. Evans and Douglas Abrams, Light on Life (Emmaus, PA: Rodale, 2005), in the discussion of arm-balancing asanas; p. 48 in the 2006 Rodale printing according to AZQuotes (page and chapter not checked in print)
meaning: Balancing on your arms trains you to accept that change never stops.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Life, 2005

quote: Without firm foundations a house cannot stand.
who: B. K. S. Iyengar, yoga teacher, Pune
source: B. K. S. Iyengar, Light on Yoga (Yoga Dipika) (London: George Allen & Unwin, 1966), Part II, 'Hints and Cautions for the Practice of Asanas', The Requisites, no. 1, p. 57
meaning: Like a house, practice needs firm foundations: good conduct and self-discipline.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966

quote: [Asanas] secure a fine physique, which is strong and elastic without being muscle bound... But their real importance lies in the way they train and discipline the mind.
who: B. K. S. Iyengar, yoga teacher, Pune
source: B. K. S. Iyengar, Light on Yoga (London: George Allen & Unwin, 1966), Part I Introduction, section 'Asana', p. 42
meaning: Asanas build a strong, supple body, but above all they train the mind.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Yoga, 1966

quote: What little bent is possible should first be secured and maintained for some time. After a while a bigger curve will become possible. In this way, with a daily practice, the spine will slowly be restored to its original state of elasticity.
who: Swami Kuvalayananda, yoga teacher and researcher, founder of Kaivalyadhama, Lonavla
source: Swami Kuvalayananda, Popular Yoga: Asanas, Part One (Lonavla: Kaivalyadhama; Bombay, 1933), ch. IV 'Cultural Poses', Halasana, 'Caution', pp. 80-81
meaning: Start small; with daily practice a stiff spine slowly becomes flexible again.

quote: The practice of Pranayama develops a steady mind, strong will-power and sound judgement.
who: B. K. S. Iyengar, yoga teacher, Pune
source: B. K. S. Iyengar, Light on Pranayama (London: George Allen & Unwin, 1981), Part One, ch. 2 'Stages of Yoga', para. 16, p. 10
meaning: Breathing practice builds a steady mind, strong will and good judgement.
credit: B. K. S. Iyengar · Light on Pranayama, 1981

quote: Every day is a good day.
who: Yunmen Wenyan (864-949), Chan (Zen) master, China
source: Blue Cliff Record (Biyan lu), case 6 (碧巖錄第六則), compiled by Yuanwu Keqin, 1125; Chinese text on Wikisource 碧巖錄/卷第一; literal translation. Dictionary: Digital Daijisen and Koji Seigo o Shiru Jiten on Kotobank (日日是好日)
meaning: Each new day, whatever it brings, can be a good day.

quote: Joshu asked Nansen: "What is the path?" Nansen said: "Everyday life is the path."
who: Nanquan (Nansen), Chan master, answering his student Zhaozhou (Joshu)
source: Wumen Huikai, The Gateless Gate (Wumenguan), case 19 '平常是道', 1228, tr. Nyogen Senzaki and Paul Reps, 1934. Japanese dictionary sense of 平常心: Digital Daijisen on Kotobank
meaning: The path is here, in your calm, ordinary, everyday mind.

quote: In caring for the body and nourishing life, take care with small things. Do not skip a small gain as not worth doing, nor ignore a small harm as harmless. Gathering small things is how you reach the great.
who: Ge Hong, Daoist writer (283-343)
source: Ge Hong, Baopuzi Neipian (The Master Who Embraces Simplicity, Inner Chapters), ch. 13 'Jiyan' (極言); literal translation
meaning: Small daily care for your body adds up to something big.

quote: ...we may find it not so interesting to cook the same thing over and over again every day... If you lose the spirit of repetition it will become quite difficult, but it will not be difficult if you are full of strength and vitality.
who: Shunryu Suzuki, Zen teacher
source: Shunryu Suzuki, Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind (1970), chapter 'Repetition', p. 55 (per the Shunryu Suzuki archive at cuke.com)
meaning: Doing the same practice every day stays easy when you bring it energy.
credit: Shunryu Suzuki · Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind

quote: Who rises early, God gives to him.
who: Russian proverb
source: V. I. Dal, Poslovitsy russkogo naroda, 1862, section 'Работа — Праздность' (Work and Idleness); literal translation. Meaning from Russian Wiktionary: 'the earlier a person gets up, the more useful things they manage to do'
meaning: Rise early, and you get more good things done.

quote: Work hard; prepare properly; some day your chance may come. If opportunity comes and you are not prepared, it may not come again.
who: John Wooden, UCLA basketball coach (1910-2010)
source: John Wooden and Steve Jamison, The Essential Wooden: A Lifetime of Lessons on Leaders and Leadership (McGraw-Hill, 2007), Part II "Preparation and Training of a Team", section "If Opportunity Knocks and You're Not Ready" (archive.org full text; page number not shown in the scan)
meaning: Prepare well now, so you are ready when your chance comes.

quote: ...the person in training must take care of both [soul and body]... the body is strengthened and becomes capable of enduring hardship, sturdy and ready for any task; the soul too is strengthened...
who: Musonius Rufus, Roman Stoic teacher (1st century AD), teacher of Epictetus
source: Lecture VI "On Training", tr. Cora E. Lutz, "Musonius Rufus: The Roman Socrates", Yale Classical Studies 10 (1947), pp. 53-55 (quoted words on p. 55)
meaning: Train body and mind together, so you grow sturdy and ready for anything.
credit: Musonius Rufus · On Training, tr. Lutz

quote: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
who: Seneca, Roman Stoic philosopher (1st century AD)
source: Moral Letters to Lucilius 13.4 ("On groundless fears"), tr. Richard M. Gummere, Loeb Classical Library vol. I, 1917
meaning: We worry about many more things than ever really happen to us.

quote: Although he never thought I would complete the race, he needed a "rabbit," someone who would go out strong and set a fast pace for the elite women.
who: Grete Waitz, distance runner, Norway
source: Grete Waitz, first-person account in Gail Waesche Kislevitz (ed.), First Marathons, Breakaway Books, New York, 1998. Excerpt 'Cool Controlled Grace' republished on MarathonGuide.com, 28 Jan 2000. World record time 2:32:30 and age 25 also in HISTORY.com Editors, 'Grete Waitz wins her eighth NYC Marathon'.
meaning: Years of daily training made her ready for a chance nobody expected.

quote: I make up exercises for myself, little chair things, turn on the radio and dance around. Use the furniture. Anything to keep the body occupied. The key is the lift of the spine.
who: Carmen de Lavallade, dancer, at 85, USA
source: Elizabeth Zimmer, 'Carmen de Lavallade Looks Back on an Extraordinary Career', The Village Voice, 24 May 2016
meaning: Keep the body moving in small ways and lift the spine, at any age.

quote: If you take care of your shoes, they take care of you.
who: Suzelle Poole, ballet dancer and teacher, at 84, Dallas, USA
source: Amelia Mugavero and ShaCamree Gowdy, 'At 84, North Texas ballerina inspires generations with lifelong passion for dance', CBS News Texas, updated 27 Oct 2024
meaning: Look after your dance shoes, and they will look after you.
credit: Suzelle Poole, at 84 · CBS News Texas, 2024

quote: During the fifth and final movement, the highest string on Midori's smaller-than-normal violin snapped. Unfazed, she borrowed concertmaster Malcolm Lowe's instrument, and when the same string on that violin also broke, she finished the performance on the violin of assistant concertmaster Max Hobart.
who: Midori (Midori Goto), violinist, aged 14, at Tanglewood, 1986
source: A. Z. Madonna, 'Seiji Ozawa's legacy shines on stage at Symphony Hall', Boston Globe, 7 Nov 2025. Confirmed by Midori's own site: 'In 1986, at the age of 14, Midori performed the Serenade with the Boston Symphony Orchestra at Tanglewood... She never missed a note.'
meaning: When her string broke twice, she stayed calm and finished the music.

quote: I slipped on the last attempt at the beginning and that's where you see your mind start to go because you can either keep persevering or you can kind of mentally give up.
who: Lynn Hill, rock climber, USA
source: Andy McCue, 'Lynn Hill - The American Legend', Climber magazine (climber.co.uk), interview at Kendal Mountain Festival, Nov 2011; page dated 1 Oct 2019
meaning: When you slip, your mind decides: keep going, or give up.

quote: Well, I advise a lot of people not to quit working. Keep busy.
who: Anthony Mancinelli, barber, aged 107, New Windsor, New York, USA
source: CBS News report from New Windsor, NY, carried by KFVS12, 26 Dec 2018. The same quote is in Jon McMichael, KOAA News5, 28 Dec 2018. Record: Guinness World Records, 'Oldest barber (male)', 107 years 220 days on 8 Oct 2018.
meaning: He cut hair five days a week at 107. His advice: keep busy.

quote: When I really do my Yoga in the morning, I have more energy in the day. I get more done. My mind is more composed.
who: Sting, musician, UK
source: Interview with Ganga White, 'Ganga Speaks with Sting About Yoga & His Life', White Lotus Foundation (sting.com lists it as Yoga Journal, Dec 1995; that page was not opened)
meaning: Morning yoga gave him more energy and a calmer mind all day.

quote: Regular leisure-time exercise of any intensity provides protection against future depression but not anxiety.
who: Samuel B. Harvey et al., King's College London, with UNSW Sydney, the Black Dog Institute and Norwegian partners (HUNT cohort, Norway)
source: Harvey SB, Øverland S, Hatch SL, Wessely S, Mykletun A, Hotopf M. Exercise and the Prevention of Depression: Results of the HUNT Cohort Study. American Journal of Psychiatry 2018;175(1):28-36. PMID 28969440. doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.2017.16111223
meaning: People who exercised regularly, even gently, were less likely to get depressed later.
credit: Harvey et al. (HUNT) · Am J Psychiatry, 2018

quote: These findings provide modest support for claims that regular exercise protects against the negative emotional consequences of stress...
who: Emma Childs and Harriet de Wit, Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neuroscience, University of Chicago
source: Childs E, de Wit H. Regular exercise is associated with emotional resilience to acute stress in healthy adults. Frontiers in Physiology 2014;5:161. PMID 24822048. PMCID PMC4013452. doi:10.3389/fphys.2014.00161
meaning: People who exercised weekly kept a better mood after a stressful test.

quote: Following the intervention, participants reported significantly reduced perceived stress. Reductions in perceived stress correlated positively with decreases in right basolateral amygdala gray matter density.
who: Britta K. Hölzel, Sara W. Lazar et al., Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School
source: Hölzel BK, Carmody J, Evans KC, et al. Stress reduction correlates with structural changes in the amygdala. Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience 2010;5(1):11-17. PMID 19776221. PMCID PMC2840837. doi:10.1093/scan/nsp034
meaning: Mindfulness eased stress in 8 weeks; those calmed most showed most brain change.

quote: ...the self-regulatory benefits of habits were apparent in the lesser feelings of stress associated with habitual than nonhabitual behavior.
who: Wendy Wood, Jeffrey M. Quinn and Deborah A. Kashy (Wood: Department of Psychology, Texas A&M University)
source: Wood W, Quinn JM, Kashy DA. Habits in everyday life: thought, emotion, and action. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 2002;83(6):1281-1297. PMID 12500811. doi:10.1037/0022-3514.83.6.1281
meaning: Things done almost daily, in the same setting, felt less stressful to people.
credit: Wood et al. · J Pers Soc Psychol, 2002

quote: As expected, yoga practitioners (i) were more accurate in assessing the rod's verticality on the RFT [rod and frame test]...
who: Francesca Fiori, Nicole David and Salvatore M. Aglioti, Sapienza University of Rome, IRCCS Fondazione Santa Lucia and University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
source: Fiori F, David N, Aglioti SM. Processing of proprioceptive and vestibular body signals and self-transcendence in Ashtanga yoga practitioners. Frontiers in Human Neuroscience 2014;8:734. PMID 25278866. PMCID PMC4166896. doi:10.3389/fnhum.2014.00734
meaning: Ashtanga practitioners judged true vertical better, less fooled by a tilted frame.
credit: Fiori et al. · Front Hum Neurosci, 2014

quote: The 12-week yoga intervention was associated with greater improvements in mood and anxiety than a metabolically matched walking exercise.
who: Chris C. Streeter et al., Division of Psychiatry, Boston University School of Medicine
source: Streeter CC, Whitfield TH, Owen L, et al. Effects of yoga versus walking on mood, anxiety, and brain GABA levels: a randomized controlled MRS study. Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine 2010;16(11):1145-1152. PMID 20722471. PMCID PMC3111147. doi:10.1089/acm.2010.0007
meaning: Twelve weeks of yoga eased worry and lifted mood more than equal-effort walking.
